title: Waves
syllabus: Wave motion, Transverse and longitudinal waves, Speed of transverse and longitudinal waves, Newton's formula and Laplace's correction, Displacement relation for a progressive wave, Principle of superposition of waves, Reflection of waves, Standing/Stationary waves in strings and organ pipes, Fundamental mode and harmonics, Beats

Fundamental frequency of open organ pipe: $
u_0 =  rac{v}{2L} = 330	ext{ Hz}$.
Fundamental frequency of closed pipe of same length: $
u_c =  rac{v}{4L} =  rac{

Third harmonic (first overtone) of closed pipe corresponds to $3
u_c$:
$$
u_3 = 3 	imes 165	ext{ Hz} = 495	ext{ Hz}$$

questions.question: Two organ pipes, one closed at one end and the other open at both ends, produce $5\text{ beats/s}$ when sounding together in their fundamental modes. If the length of the open pipe is $100\text{ cm}$, the length of the closed pipe may be: (Speed of sound $= 340\text{ m/s}$) (NEET 2020)
questions.solution:
Fundamental of open pipe: $\nu_o = \frac{v}{2L_o} = \frac{340}{2(1.0)} = 170\text{ Hz}$.
Fundamental of closed pipe: $\nu_c = \frac{v}{4L_c} = 170 \pm 5 = 175\text{ Hz}$ or $165\text{ Hz}$.
1) $L_c = \frac{340}{4 \times 175} = \frac{340}{700} \approx 0.4857\text{ m} = 48.6\text{ cm}$ (or for $2\nu_c$: $24.2\text{ cm}$).
2) $L_c = \frac{340}{4 \times 165} = \frac{340}{660} \approx 0.515\text{ m} = 51.5\text{ cm}$.
For fundamental mode quarter-length relation, $L_c = \frac{v}{4\nu_c} = 48.6\text{ cm}$ or $51.5\text{ cm}$ (or $25.8\text{ cm} / 24.2\text{ cm}$ when compared to half-wave basis).

questions.question: A tuning fork is used to produce resonance in a glass tube. The resonance is observed at two successive lengths $20\text{ cm}$ and $62\text{ cm}$ of the water column. The end correction of the tube is: (NEET 2018)
questions.solution:
Resonance conditions with end correction $e$:
$l_1 + e = \frac{\lambda}{4} = 20 + e$
$l_2 + e = \frac{3\lambda}{4} = 62 + e$
$$(l_2 + e) = 3(l_1 + e) \implies 62 + e = 3(20 + e) = 60 + 3e \implies 2e = 2 \implies e = 1.0\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: A tuning fork with frequency $800\text{ Hz}$ produces resonance in a resonance column tube with upper end open and lower end closed by water surface. Successive resonances are observed at lengths $9.75\text{ cm}$, $31.25\text{ cm}$, and $52.75\text{ cm}$. The speed of sound in air is: (NEET 2019)
questions.solution:
Difference between successive resonance lengths is $\frac{\lambda}{2}$:
$$\frac{\lambda}{2} = l_2 - l_1 = 31.25 - 9.75 = 21.50\text{ cm} = 0.215\text{ m} \implies \lambda = 0.43\text{ m}$$
$$v = \nu \lambda = 800\text{ Hz} \times 0.43\text{ m} = 344\text{ m/s}$$

questions.solution:

u_c =  rac{v}{4L_c}$.

questions.question: A string of mass $2.5\text{ kg}$ is under a tension of $200\text{ N}$. The length of the stretched string is $20\text{ m}$. If the transverse jerk is struck at one end of the string, the time taken for the disturbance to reach the other end is: (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
Linear mass density $\mu = \frac{m}{L} = \frac{2.5\text{ kg}}{20\text{ m}} = 0.125\text{ kg/m}$.
Wave speed $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{200}{0.125}} = \sqrt{1600} = 40\text{ m/s}$.
$$\text{Time } t = \frac{L}{v} = \frac{20\text{ m}}{40\text{ m/s}} = 0.5\text{ s}$$

questions.question: A wave travelling in the $+x$-direction having maximum displacement along $y$-direction as $1\text{ m}$, wavelength $2\pi\text{ m}$ and frequency $\frac{1}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$ is represented by: (NEET 2013)
questions.solution:
Amplitude $A = 1\text{ m}$.
Wave number $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} = \frac{2\pi}{2\pi} = 1\text{ m}^{-1}$.
Angular frequency $\omega = 2\pi\nu = 2\pi\left(\frac{1}{\pi}\right) = 2\text{ rad/s}$.
For wave traveling along $+x$ direction: $y = A\sin(kx - \omega t) = \sin(x - 2t)$.

questions.question: When a sound wave travels from air into water, which of the following physical quantities remains UNCHANGED?
questions.solution: Frequency is a characteristic of the vibrating source producing the wave and remains strictly constant when a wave transitions across different propagating media.

questions.question: Newton's formula for the velocity of sound in a gaseous medium was modified by Laplace by assuming that compression and rarefaction occur:
questions.solution: Newton assumed isothermal conditions ($v = \sqrt{P/\rho}$). Laplace corrected this by pointing out that compressions and rarefactions occur so rapidly and gases are such poor thermal conductors that heat exchange is zero, making the process adiabatic ($v = \sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}$).

questions.question: A stationary wave is represented by $y = 2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t)$. The distance between a node and its adjacent antinode is:
questions.solution: In a standing wave, the distance between two consecutive nodes or two consecutive antinodes is $\lambda/2$. The distance between an adjacent node and antinode is $\lambda/4$.

questions.question: Two sound waves are given by $y_1 = A\sin(1000\pi t)$ and $y_2 = A\sin(1008\pi t)$. The number of beats heard per second is:
questions.solution:
$\omega_1 = 1000\pi \implies 
u_1 =  rac{1000\pi}{2\pi} = 500	ext{ Hz}$.

$$	ext{Beat frequency } 
u_{	ext{beat}} = |

questions.question: The speed of sound in hydrogen gas at STP is $v$. The speed of sound in oxygen gas at STP will be: (Assume both are diatomic with same $\gamma$)
questions.solution: $$v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}} \implies \frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{v_{\text{H}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{\text{H}_2}}{M_{\text{O}_2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{32}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{16}} = \frac{1}{4} \implies v_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{v}{4}$$

questions.question: In a stretched string fixed at both ends, the ratio of the frequencies of the fundamental, second harmonic, and third harmonic is:
questions.solution:
For a string fixed at both ends: $\nu_n = n\left(\frac{v}{2L}\right)$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$.
Thus, the harmonics are in the integral ratio $1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : \dots$.

questions.question: In a closed organ pipe (closed at one end), which harmonics are present in the acoustic spectrum?
questions.solution: A closed pipe supports resonant standing waves with a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end: $\nu_n = (2n - 1)\frac{v}{4L}$ ($n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$). Only odd harmonics ($1, 3, 5, 7, \dots$) are produced.

questions.question: A sound wave is reflected from a rigid fixed boundary. The phase change introduced upon reflection is:
questions.solution: When a mechanical wave is reflected from a denser medium or rigid boundary, a phase reversal of $\pi\text{ rad}$ ($180^\circ$) occurs in the displacement wave.

questions.question: If the tension in a stretched string is increased by $69\%$, the percentage increase in the speed of transverse waves on the string is:
questions.solution:
$v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} \implies \frac{v'}{v} = \sqrt{\frac{1.69T}{T}} = \sqrt{1.69} = 1.30$.
$$\%\Delta v = (1.30 - 1) \times 100\% = 30\%$$

questions.question: The displacement of a wave is given by $y = 4\sin\left[2\pi\left(\frac{t}{0.04} - \frac{x}{50}\right)\right]$, where $x$ and $y$ are in $\text{cm}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$. The wave speed is:
questions.solution:
$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{0.04} = 50\pi\text{ rad/s}$ and $k = \frac{2\pi}{50} = \frac{\pi}{25}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
$$v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{50\pi}{\pi/25} = 50 \times 25 = 1250\text{ cm/s}$$

questions.question: A tuning fork $A$ produces $4\text{ beats/s}$ with another tuning fork $B$ of frequency $256\text{ Hz}$. When fork $A$ is loaded with a small amount of wax, the beat frequency decreases to $2\text{ beats/s}$. The original frequency of fork $A$ is:
questions.solution:
Possible frequencies for $A$: $
u_A = 256 \pm 4 = 260	ext{ Hz}$ or $252	ext{ Hz}$.
Loading with wax decreases the frequency of $A$ ($
u_A \downarrow$).
If $
u_A = 260	ext{ Hz}$, decreasing it causes the beat frequency $|
u_A - 256|$ to decrease towards 2 (satisfies the condition).
If $
u_A = 252	ext{ Hz}$, decreasing it would increase the beat frequency to $>4$.
Hence, original frequency is $260	ext{ Hz}$.

questions.question: The equation of a progressive wave is $y = 0.2\cos\pi\left(0.04t + 0.02x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ (SI units). The phase difference between two points separated by a distance of $0.5\text{ m}$ along the propagation direction is:
questions.solution:
Propagation constant $k = 0.02\pi\text{ m}^{-1}$.
$$\Delta\phi = k \Delta x = (0.02\pi) \times 0.5 = 0.01\pi\text{ rad}$$

questions.question: Which of the following statements about standing waves is FALSE?
options: Energy is transmitted continuously along the medium
Particles at nodes are permanently at rest
All particles between two consecutive nodes vibrate in the same phase
Amplitude varies with position along the wave
questions.solution: In a stationary/standing wave, energy is confined between nodes and is not propagated forward through the medium.

questions.question: An open pipe of length $L$ resonates at its fundamental frequency. If one end is now closed, the fundamental frequency of the closed pipe will be:
questions.solution:
Open pipe fundamental: $
u_o =  rac{v}{2L}$.
Closed pipe fundamental: $
u_c =  rac{v}{4L} =  rac{
u_o}{2}$ (halved).

questions.question: A transverse wave is described by $y = A\sin(\omega t - kx)$. The maximum particle velocity is equal to four times the wave velocity if:
questions.solution:
Maximum particle velocity $v_{p,\text{max}} = A\omega$.
Wave propagation speed $v = \frac{\omega}{k}$.
$$A\omega = 4\left(\frac{\omega}{k}\right) \implies A = \frac{4}{k} = \frac{4}{2\pi/\lambda} = \frac{2\lambda}{\pi} \implies \lambda = \frac{\pi A}{2}$$

questions.question: A stretched string of length $L$ vibrates in 4 loops (4 segments). The wavelength $\lambda$ of the stationary wave is:
questions.solution:
Length of string vibrating in $p$ loops: $L = p\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right)$.
For $p = 4$:
$$L = 4\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) = 2\lambda \implies \lambda = \frac{L}{2}$$

questions.question: How does the speed of sound in an ideal gas change when the pressure is doubled at constant temperature?
questions.solution: Speed of sound $v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}$. At constant temperature, $P/\rho$ remains constant (Boyle's law), so sound velocity is completely independent of pressure changes.

questions.question: The ratio of velocities of sound in dry air and moist air at the same temperature and pressure is:
questions.solution: Water vapor has lower molar mass ($18\text{ g/mol}$) than dry air ($\approx 29\text{ g/mol}$), making moist air less dense than dry air ($\rho_{\text{moist}} < \rho_{\text{dry}}$). Since $v \propto 1/\sqrt{\rho}$, sound travels faster in moist air ($v_{\text{dry}} < v_{\text{moist}}$).

questions.question: A sonometer wire of length $100\text{ cm}$ has a fundamental frequency of $300\text{ Hz}$. Where should two bridges be placed to divide the wire into three segments whose fundamental frequencies are in the ratio $1 : 2 : 3$?
options: At $54.55\text{ cm}$ and $81.82\text{ cm}$ from one end
questions.solution:
Since $\nu \propto 1/L$, the lengths of the segments are in the ratio $L_1 : L_2 : L_3 = 1 : \frac{1}{2} : \frac{1}{3} = 6 : 3 : 2$.
$L_1 = \frac{6}{11} \times 100\text{ cm} \approx 54.55\text{ cm}$.
$L_2 = \frac{3}{11} \times 100\text{ cm} \approx 27.27\text{ cm}$.
Bridges are placed at $x_1 = 54.55\text{ cm}$ and $x_2 = 54.55 + 27.27 = 81.82\text{ cm}$.

questions.question: Two waves represented by $y_1 = 3\sin(kx - \omega t)$ and $y_2 = 4\cos(kx - \omega t)$ interfere. The amplitude of the resultant wave is:
questions.solution:
Rewriting $y_2 = 4\sin\left(kx - \omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Phase difference is $\phi = 90^\circ$.
$$A_{\text{res}} = \sqrt{A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2A_1 A_2 \cos 90^\circ} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$$

questions.question: The equation of a stationary wave on a string is $y = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{3}\right)\cos(20\pi t)$ where $x, y$ are in $\text{cm}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$. The distance between two successive nodes is:
questions.solution:
Wave number $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies \lambda = 6\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Distance between consecutive nodes} = \frac{\lambda}{2} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: An open pipe of length $33\text{ cm}$ resonates with frequency $1000\text{ Hz}$ in a certain harmonic. If speed of sound in air is $330\text{ m/s}$, which harmonic is excited?
questions.solution:
Fundamental of open pipe: $
u_1 =  rac{v}{2L} =  rac{330}{2 	imes 0.33} = 500	ext{ Hz}$.
Given $
u = 1000	ext{ Hz} = 2 	imes 500	ext{ Hz} = 2
u_1$.
Thus, it corresponds to the second harmonic (first overtone).

questions.question: A sound absorber attenuates the sound level by $20\text{ dB}$. The intensity of sound decreases by a factor of:
questions.solution: $$\Delta L = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{I_1}{I_2}\right) = 20 \implies \log_{10}\left(\frac{I_1}{I_2}\right) = 2 \implies \frac{I_1}{I_2} = 10^2 = 100$$

questions.question: Which of the following types of waves CANNOT be polarized?
questions.solution: Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves where particle oscillations occur along the direction of propagation. Only transverse waves can exhibit polarization.

questions.question: Two waves with intensities in the ratio $9 : 1$ interfere. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the interference pattern is:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \sqrt{\frac{I_1}{I_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{1}} = 3$$
$$\frac{I_{\text{max}}}{I_{\text{min}}} = \left(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{3 + 1}{3 - 1}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{4}{2}\right)^2 = 2^2 = 4 : 1$$

questions.question: A transverse wave travels along a wire of tension $T$ and linear density $\mu$. The average power transmitted along the string is:
questions.solution: The time-averaged rate of energy transfer (power) in a sinusoidal transverse string wave is $P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{2} \mu v \omega^2 A^2$.

questions.question: A tuning fork $P$ of frequency $250\text{ Hz}$ produces $5\text{ beats/s}$ with another fork $Q$. When $Q$ is filed slightly, the beat frequency becomes $2\text{ beats/s}$. The frequency of $Q$ before filing was:
questions.solution:
Initial possibilities for $Q$: $250 \pm 5 = 255\text{ Hz}$ or $245\text{ Hz}$.
Filing a tuning fork removes mass and increases its frequency ($\nu_Q \uparrow$).
If $\nu_Q = 245\text{ Hz}$, increasing it brings it closer to $250\text{ Hz}$ (e.g., $248\text{ Hz}$), reducing the beat frequency to $2\text{ beats/s}$.
Thus, initial frequency was $245\text{ Hz}$.

questions.question: The temperature at which the speed of sound in air becomes double its value at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$v \propto \sqrt{T} \implies \frac{v_T}{v_0} = \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}} = 2 \implies \frac{T}{273} = 4 \implies T = 1092\text{ K}$$
$$T = (1092 - 273)^\circ\text{C} = 819^\circ\text{C}$$

questions.question: For a wave propagating along the x-axis, the relation between particle velocity $v_p$ and wave velocity $v$ at any point is:
questions.solution:
For $y = f(x - vt)$:
Particle velocity $v_p = \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} = -v f'(x - vt)$.
Slope of wave shape $= \frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = f'(x - vt)$.
$$v_p = -v \left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\right)$$

questions.question: If an open pipe and a closed pipe have the same fundamental frequency, the ratio of their lengths $L_o / L_c$ is:
questions.solution: $$\nu_o = \nu_c \implies \frac{v}{2L_o} = \frac{v}{4L_c} \implies 2L_o = 4L_c \implies \frac{L_o}{L_c} = 2 : 1$$

questions.question: The displacement of a particle in a medium is given by $y = 10^{-4}\sin(100t + 20x + \pi/4)\text{ m}$. The wave travels along:
questions.solution:
The form $(\omega t + kx)$ indicates propagation along the negative x-direction.
Speed $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{100}{20} = 5\text{ m/s}$.

questions.question: In a resonance tube apparatus, if end correction is accounted for with pipe diameter $D$, the value of end correction $e$ is approximately:
questions.solution: Lord Rayleigh's end correction formula states $e \approx 0.6 r = 0.3 D$, where $r$ is internal radius and $D$ is diameter.

questions.question: A steel wire has a length of $12.0\text{ m}$ and a mass of $2.40\text{ kg}$. What is the tension in the wire if the speed of a transverse wave on the wire is $60.0\text{ m/s}$?
questions.solution:
$\mu = \frac{2.40\text{ kg}}{12.0\text{ m}} = 0.20\text{ kg/m}$.
$$T = \mu v^2 = (0.20\text{ kg/m}) \times (60.0\text{ m/s})^2 = 0.20 \times 3600 = 720\text{ N}$$

questions.question: The phase difference between two vibrating particles separated by path difference $\Delta x$ in a wave of wavelength $\lambda$ is:
questions.solution: The fundamental relation between phase difference and path difference is $\Delta\phi = k \Delta x = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$.

questions.question: A string of length $L$ fixed at both ends resonates in $n$ loops. The positions of nodes measured from one fixed end are:
questions.solution: For $n$ loops, the loop length is $L/n$. Nodes occur at $x = m\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) = m\left(\frac{L}{n}\right)$ for $m = 0, 1, 2, \dots, n$.

questions.question: A sound wave of frequency $\nu$ travels through a gas of adiabatic index $\gamma$ and density $\rho$ under pressure $P$. Its wavelength is:
questions.solution: Wave speed $v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}$. Wavelength $\lambda = \frac{v}{\nu} = \frac{1}{\nu}\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}$.

questions.question: The intensity $I$ of a spherical wave expanding outward uniformly from a point source in a non-absorbing medium varies with distance $r$ as:
questions.solution: By energy conservation over concentric spherical wave fronts: $P = I(4\pi r^2) = \text{constant} \implies I = \frac{P}{4\pi r^2} \propto \frac{1}{r^2}$.

questions.question: Standing waves are produced by the superposition of two waves traveling in:
options: Opposite directions with equal amplitude and equal frequency
Same direction with equal amplitude and equal frequency
Opposite directions with slightly different frequencies
questions.solution: Standing waves result from the interference of two identical harmonic waves possessing equal frequency and amplitude traveling in mutually opposite directions along the same line.
